Checking that against the transcripts. `preamble7.md` describes itself as replacing all earlier preambles, so I need to see what happened to it after claude-4 wrote it:preamble7 was written at 05:39 on 10-06 and sent with at least three packets before the outage. Checking what you said about it in that window:㊟ ("only preamble 6 is current") The transcripts suggest preamble 7 was the current one when the drive failed.
- At 05:39 on 10-06 you told claude-4: "please update the instructions you give out accordingly and mint new seats to avoid confusion". That was after its WHY note proposed the instruction changes "for Joe to decide".
- In the same minute claude-4 wrote `preamble7.md`, which begins "This preamble replaces all earlier ones". It then sent it with the packets for the new seats it had just created: `hdrcensus` to codex-34, `epslevels` to codex-35 and `sigreaders` to codex-34. That was its last dispatch round before the drive died at 09:45.
- It also updated its own status line to "Rules: preamble7.md governs".
- You didn't send claude-4 anything else between then and the outage.

So preamble 6 was current until 05:39 on 10-06; it ran from 21:42 on 10-04. Preamble 7 is the update you asked for at 05:39, and it ran for the last four hours.

🈯 (which do you mean?) Should the instructions be preamble 6, with preamble 7's rules set aside? Or did you mean the latest one, whatever its number?
- If preamble 6, I'll ask zai-1 to rebuild it. It was assembled by a shell command from preamble 5 plus additions, and the transcripts have every step. Then I'll make it the current file and mark 7 as superseded in the README.
- If you meant 7, nothing needs to change.
